findings.evidence: A third construction on the rate-limit concept. The shipped fr corpus writes it as «limite de débit» (9 values, e.g. ui.chat.error_block.rate_limit.before) and «{host} limité en débit» (ui.code_review.host.cooling). Noun-first «Débit audio limité» reads first as an audio-bitrate cap in a card whose subject is audio. Not misleading — the sentence below («La génération audio est très sollicitée en ce moment.») names the condition — and the class stays distinct from the other five.
findings.suggested: «Audio limité en débit» (21 cells, keeps the corpus construction and its own word «débit»), or keep as is and let the sentence below disambiguate.

findings.current: Règlement en attente — … / Vérification du règlement.
findings.evidence: «règlement» has 0 occurrences in the shipped fr catalogue (467 keys) and no glossary row, so it is a new programme term introduced silently; it is also the homonym of «règlement» = rules, which is the weaker reading of «Vérification du règlement.» in isolation. The corpus states the same pending-charge fact with «frais finaux non confirmés» (ui.chat.canonical.sound.cost.estimated_zero). Both keys use «règlement» consistently, so nothing collides inside the slice.
findings.suggested: Either record settlement → «règlement» as a glossary row (then both keys stand), or align to the corpus family: «Frais finaux en attente — les frais finaux apparaîtront dès que le fournisseur les aura communiqués.» / «Vérification des frais.»
